title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2610.37380v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences. We formulate Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts an existing explanation to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity. Rather than relying on reader-written reference explanations, we learn personalized rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. However, this presents two challenges: distinguishing persona-specific preferences from general explanation quality and learning beyond a limited set of predefined explanation styles. To address these challenges, we propose Personalized Explanation Rewriting via Preference Learning (PERPL), a framework consisting of two components. translated_title: 同样的结论，不同的读者：基于相对偏好的个性化事实核查解释
translated_abstract: 事实核查解释帮助网络用户理解某个声明为何得到其核查结论，然而同一种解释可能无法满足具有不同背景和偏好的读者。我们提出了“忠实个性化事实核查解释改写”这一任务，即在保持事实忠实性的前提下，将现有解释改写以适应个体读者。我们不依赖读者撰写的参考解释，而是从大语言模型模拟读者的相对偏好中学习个性化改写。然而，这带来了两个挑战：如何将特定角色的偏好与一般解释质量区分开来，以及如何在有限的预定义解释风格之外进行学习。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了基于偏好学习的个性化解释改写框架PERPL，该框架由两个组件构成。其中，模拟偏好构建通过交叉比较（原文此处截断）从模拟读者的相对偏好中获取角色特定的监督信号。
tldr: 提出PERPL框架，利用LLM模拟读者的相对偏好来学习个性化的事实核查解释改写，在保持事实忠实性的同时满足不同背景读者的需求。
en_tdlr: Proposes PERPL, a framework that learns personalized fact-checking explanation rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers, adapting explanations to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity.
